bullets.title: Broad tech/semis selloff deepens: SPX 6-day losing streak, VIX ~30, NDX -1.9% pre-market
bullets.body: The S&P 500 is on its sixth consecutive down session with futures -0.67% to -1.0%, Nasdaq futures -1.2% to -1.9%, and VIX at 29-30 (highest since the March Iran war). Asian markets led declines with Nikkei and Kospi both -5%+ overnight, Taiwan -6.2%. Semis saw the worst of it: SOX -10.2% over five days, SMH -3.5% Thursday, with AMD -6.5-7.7%, NVDA -3.3%, MU -5.0%, INTC -4.6%, and networking names (LITE, COHR, CIEN, MRVL) all -5-6% pre-market.

bullets.title: Fed hawkish pivot — market now pricing inflation-first stance, possible 50bp hike as early as December
bullets.body: Fed officials are now explicitly prioritizing a return to 2% core PCE over growth, a shift that wasn't priced in when investors assumed comfort with ~2.5% inflation. Cleveland Fed's Paulson backed further rate hikes; Chicago Fed's Goolsbee kept options open. Some commentary flagged a possible 50bp hike at the December FOMC, though UBS sees 25bp in Dec/Jan as the base case with 5% as ceiling on 2yr rates. The hawkish turn is the principal macro catalyst behind the current risk-off move, per multiple strategists.

bullets.title: AI capex-peak narrative driving derating; semis HF net exposure at lowest since Sept 2025
bullets.body: China tech giants (Tencent flagging 2027 capex peak, Alibaba moderating spend in 2H28) crystallized investor fears that hyperscaler AI capex will decelerate in 2028-29. Hedge funds have been net sellers of semis for 6 consecutive weeks — the longest streak on record — with global HF net semi exposure down 67% from YTD peak. JPM International notes the recovery is more likely H-shaped than V-shaped given peaking capex expectations and policy/funding headwinds, though tactically the setup screens as extreme on multiple valuation metrics.

bullets.title: US export controls on AI chips broaden: TSMC/Samsung pausing China consumer chip shipments at ≤16nm
bullets.body: TSMC is complying with new US rules on Chinese chip designers and, alongside Samsung, has paused consumer chip shipments to China at 16nm and below. Commerce approved ~880k Nvidia/AMD advanced AI chips to Chinese firms including some military-linked entities. The MATCH Act and related semiconductor export control bills (AI OVERWATCH, Chip Security Act) are odds-on for NDAA inclusion per Wolfe Research, with legislative clarity potentially a catalyst for sentiment reversal in early 2027.

bullets.title: 10yr yield at 4.97-4.99%, bonds rallying; copper -8% weekly; commodities crashing
bullets.body: The 10yr UST broke 5.07% to the downside and is now rallying, with yields -6-8bps on the session to ~4.97-4.99%. Copper is down more than 8% on the week to March lows; oil is down for a third straight week as the geopolitical risk premium unwinds. Hedgeye has pivoted from short bonds to long TLT on the commodity crash signal, while multiple strategists recommend being long duration during what they characterize as a non-recessionary Fed-induced slowdown.

bullets.title: Mutual fund positioning: Mag7 underweight 722bp, cash at record-low 1.1%; AI infra adds accelerated in Q3
bullets.body: GS analysis of 453 large-cap mutual funds ($3.9T AUM) shows funds were 722bp underweight Mag7 at Q3-end with AMZN the only constituent held overweight — its first overweight since 2016. Cash balances hit a record-low 1.1% of assets. Funds narrowed their AI-exposed equity underweight from 175bp to 130bp in Q3, adding most aggressively to AMD, PLTR, SNDK, and WDC. New overweight additions include CRM and NET; new underweights include NFLX and CSCO.

bullets.title: Hyperscalers forecast FCF-negative through 2028 with ~$595bn funding gap; $450bn AI supply expected in 2027
bullets.body: JPM credit research projects the hyperscaler group will be FCF-negative in aggregate through 2028 with a ~$595bn funding gap across 2027-28. AWS is guiding ~40% growth; Google Cloud faces a growing opportunity as Search slows. JPM expects ~$450bn in AI-related USD supply in 2027 split between parent-level hyperscaler issuance and GPU/data center financing. JPM moved Alphabet to Neutral from Overweight on tighter valuations and Search durability concerns while remaining Overweight Amazon and Oracle.

bullets.title: China SPE imports +24% YoY in Oct; non-litho (deposition +83%, etch +69%) surging, litho down 39%
bullets.body: China semiconductor process equipment imports reached $3.7bn in October (+24% YoY), but the mix is shifting sharply away from lithography (down 39% YoY to $633m, with 10M26 cumulative -15%) toward deposition (record $1.1bn, +83%) and etch ($1.1bn, +69%). UBS sees no evidence of litho stockpiling despite MATCH Act concerns, and notes ASML's China revenue is guided to normalize to ~20% of group sales. UBS remains constructive on China WFE demand.

bullets.title: Korea/Taiwan tech activity cooling — leading indicator for US semis weakness
bullets.body: Korea's semiconductor exports are ~26% of GDP and output has surged ~200% since 2023, but confidence, PMIs, and equity shares are now declining — signaling an unsustainable trajectory. Taiwan was down ~18% for the week (worst since January 1991) and Korea -5.2%. Jefferies EM quant downgrades both markets for 2027, shifting toward India and high-ROIC quality names. Bank of Korea is supporting a weak won with rate hikes.

bullets.title: INTU down ~10% on Credit Karma guidance cut to +3-7% from +11-13%; Mailchimp sold for $3.68B
bullets.body: Intuit beat F1Q27 revenue ($4.35B, +1.2% vs consensus) and EPS ($2.91, +18% vs consensus), but cut FY27 Credit Karma growth guidance dramatically to 3-7% from 11-13%, citing higher rates and a faster-than-expected consumer shift to AI-powered financial discovery tools. Full-year revenue guidance was trimmed to +8-9% (from +9-10%). Intuit also announced the sale of Mailchimp for $3.68B (a ~70% discount to its ~$12B purchase price), with proceeds earmarked for buybacks. GBSG grew +15% and mid-market momentum remains strong.

bullets.title: GOOGL Gemini cadence accelerates: 3 models in <1 month; Tasks agent live for 1B+ users
bullets.body: Google released three Gemini 4 models in under a month (Carbon, Hydrogen, Neon), with Neon ranking #3 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 32% lower cost than Carbon. Hydrogen now powers Search globally. Gemini Tasks — a free consumer AI agent — launched Nov 17 across 6 countries with capabilities including local calls, bill analysis, and tokenized Google Pay checkouts, providing a direct agentic commerce monetization path. JPM reiterates Overweight with a $375 Dec-27 PT at 22x 2028E GAAP EPS of $17.

bullets.title: AI chip export controls legislation on track for NDAA; MATCH Act unlikely to mean blanket DUV ban
bullets.body: Wolfe Research sees three semiconductor export control bills (AI OVERWATCH, MATCH, Chip Security Act) as odds-on for NDAA inclusion, with the Remote Access Security Act also possible. However, UBS notes MATCH Act does not constitute a blanket DUV ban to China, and legislative clarity by year-end could trigger a sentiment reversal in semis in early 2027. No evidence the White House is pushing to remove the MATCH Act to preserve a US-China trade truce.

bullets.title: S&P 500 3Q26 earnings: 33% EPS growth on track, 77% beat rate; Big Tech mixed with NVDA +104% vs GOOGL -6%
bullets.body: With ~98% of S&P 500 market cap reported, 3Q26 is tracking to 14.8% revenue growth and 32.9% EPS growth with a 77% beat rate and 5.8% aggregate EPS beat. NVDA actual EPS growth of 104.5% beat the 88.9% expectation; MSFT +18.3% vs +14.4% expected; AAPL +9.0% vs +5.5%. On the miss side: GOOGL -5.8% vs +6.3% expected and AMZN -2.0% vs +2.0% expected. S&P 500 2026 YTD returns remain below average despite record EPS, with multiples contracting on macro/AI concerns.

bullets.title: JPM tactically bullish despite selloff; reiterates SPX 8,000 YE26 target, $365 EPS at 21.9x
bullets.body: JPM US Market Intelligence is tactically bullish on the tech rebound, noting positioning has flushed to the ~20th percentile on their tactical monitor. They reiterate SPX 8,000 year-end 2026 target. Global semis positioning is at the 80th percentile, suggesting room for further downside, but SOX is approaching multi-year valuation lows with TD Combo Buy Counts near 13-day triggers — 73% of SOX names near Buy signals. Recommend tactically bullish approach via Mag7 and options on AI themes.

bullets.title: US holiday e-commerce projected +10% YoY; AMZN and SHOP best ideas with agentic commerce emerging
bullets.body: JPM projects US e-commerce holiday growth of ~+10% Y/Y, reaching ~27% of adjusted retail sales (+100bps Y/Y). Amazon guides 4Q retail revenue +9.7% FXN and Shopify guides +33% FXN. AI-driven retail traffic grew +71% Y/Y per Adobe; Shopify's agentic traffic grew +2.6x Y/Y in 3Q with ~64% higher conversion vs organic search. Chase card data shows +11% card-not-present spending growth 4QTD. AMZN and SHOP are JPM's top ideas.

bullets.title: Consumer staples (XLP) at 15% premium to S&P 500 — widest since Dec 2022; valuation now a headwind
bullets.body: XLP has outperformed the S&P 500 for 7 consecutive weeks but now trades at ~15% premium — the widest gap since December 2022. UBS flags that further outperformance requires positive estimate revisions and proof of broadening growth; valuation no longer provides support. Morgan Stanley notes consumption remains resilient but faces near-term moderation from soft real income growth in 2027-28.

bullets.title: French/Italian political risk on radar: Le Pen ~92%+ odds; Italy hung-parliament risk rising into 2027
bullets.body: Le Pen holds a ~92-100% statistical probability of winning France's second round depending on the opponent; a court eligibility ruling is due early April. The France 10Y-Bund spread is at ~150bp with market pressure expected to discipline any RN spending plans. In Italy, autumn 2027 is the base case for elections but spring 2027 risk is material; both centre-right (42.5%) and centre-left (44.7%) blocs hover near the 42% majority threshold required to avoid proportional representation.

bullets.title: BoE likely delays next hike to February; UK Oct retail sales +0.7% beat but consumer outlook soft
bullets.body: UK CPI came in softer than BoE forecast at 3.6% (vs 3.7% expected) and PAYE payrolls unexpectedly dropped 34k in October, strengthening the case to delay tightening to February. Retail sales rebounded 0.7% m/m in October, though boosted by government stockpiling. Underlying consumer spending is expected to soften in 4Q; GfK confidence recovered only 2pts to -22, well below neutral.

bullets.title: JPM 2027 Treasury demand: ~$1.38T across buyers; bill-heavy mix limits duration pressure
bullets.body: JPM forecasts 2027 Treasury demand of ~$1.38T: Fed $180bn (all T-bills), Foreign $550bn (skewed short), Banks $100bn (asset swaps), Pensions $100bn, Mutual Funds/ETFs $300bn, and MMFs $250bn in T-bills. The bill-heavy funding mix reduces duration pressure despite a wider headline supply/demand gap. Near two-decade-high real yields are attracting mutual fund/ETF demand, with that bucket expected to rise as elevated equity valuations prompt reallocation.

bullets.title: Agentic AI reshaping enterprise software pricing: SAP, Dassault moving to output/consumption models; operating leverage by 2H27
bullets.body: MS European TMT conference takeaway: software vendors have moved from early-stage AI exploration to mature agentic product roadmaps. SAP plans autonomous enterprise workflows across Finance and HR with a dedicated AI revenue KPI launching January 2027; Dassault is using Blue tokens (output-based pricing); Nemetschek combines subscriptions with consumption credits. Management teams now openly discuss AI-driven headcount reductions, with Dassault expecting AI to halve incremental hiring and SAP expecting net headcount declines. Operating leverage expected to materialize in 2H27.
